nodes.hint_edit: Biopsy of an eye that still contains the tumour is avoided, because incisional or needle biopsy risks seeding the tumour outside the eye. A pathology report therefore exists only once the eye itself has been removed as treatment. B-scan ultrasound and orbital magnetic resonance imaging are not available everywhere, so the next step records which imaging was actually performed.

options.label_head: Referral letter or clinical note only — no ophthalmic examination or i
options.rationale: Lowest tier. Fits every set with no Imaging Report, Cytology or Histology Report, so a lone Lab Report, IHC Report or Gene report, or nothing ticked, lands here. Mirrors the label's three 'no' clauses.

options.label_head: Ophthalmic examination under anaesthesia, B-scan ultrasound, and/or or
options.rationale: Imaging Report ticked with no cytology and no pathology report, as the label states. Lab, IHC and genetics ticked beside imaging do not change the tier. 'Eye is intact' follows from the absence of a Histology Report.

options.label_head: Cytology report, or an aqueous-humour or plasma liquid biopsy report —
options.rationale: Requires the Cytology document itself (aqueous-humour or liquid-biopsy cytology is in its definition). IHC beside Cytology stays here as immunocytochemistry. Excludes Histology Report because the label says no enucleation or exenteration specimen is in the file; a set with Histology falls to the tissue tier.

options.label_head: Enucleation or exenteration specimen with a pathology report
options.rationale: The label asserts a pathology report on a tissue specimen, so it requires the Histology Report document. Histology outranks Cytology and Imaging. IHC or genetics alone never reach this tier.

options.label_head: A specimen (cytology, or enucleation/exenteration) was obtained but is
options.rationale: States a quality finding (inadequate, non-diagnostic or uninterpretable specimen) that no document id can express. Always available, carries no tick rules.

nodes.hint_was: Pick the highest tier of evidence genuinely in the file. There is no 'histology' or 'biopsy' option for an intact eye: incisional or needle biopsy of an eye that still contains the tumour risks seeding it outside the eye, so a pathology report exists only once the eye itself has been removed as treatment. B-scan ultrasound and orbital magnetic resonance imaging are not available everywhere -- record which imaging was actually performed, at the next step.
